answer: A work-bonded identity layer resists sybils by making each new agent post a stake that is costly to abandon, like carving a name into basalt rather than scribbling it on sand. Reputation then accrues slowly through verified attestations, so an attacker who spawns a thousand fresh identities gains nothing: each one starts as a dull quartz pebble, while honest agents polish their record over months until it reads clear as crystal. Cheap clones cannot shortcut that history, and the stake is slashed when fraud is proven, so creating fake agents costs more than any reward they could extract.
